question: How do I start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages?
expected: Recommend chulapa-101 as a personal blog template; create repository, enable Settings > Pages > GitHub Actions, set title/description/author/repository/url and commit to main or master. Workflow supplies base path; no local install or personal token required. Cite /docs/00-start directly; preserve settings and check the separate index.html heading and edited sample article publicly.

result.answer:
To start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages, use the Chulapa 101 template. Follow these steps:

1.  **Generate the template**: Use the [Chulapa 101 template](https://github.com/dieghernan/chulapa-101/generate).
2.  **Configure Settings**: In your GitHub repository, go to **Settings > Pages** and ensure GitHub Actions is selected for your deployment.
3.  **Customize Content**: Edit the following files in your repository:
    *   `_config.yml`: Update section A with your `title`, `description`, `author`, `repository`, and `url`.
    *   `index.html`: Update the title and sample article content.
    *   `_posts/`: Replace sample articles with your own.
    *   `assets/img/`: Upload your own images and update article references.
4.  **Publish**: Commit your changes to the publishing branch (e.g., `main` or `master`). Wait for the GitHub Actions workflow to succeed, then verify your live site via **Settings > Pages**.

Sources:
* [Installation guide](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/01-install)
* [Basic editing and publishing](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/00-start)

question: How do I embed a local MP4 video? Give the Liquid include.
expected: snippets/video.html fileurl. Use a root-relative fileurl without relative_url or a manually added baseurl; the snippet applies absolute_url. Include a public playback check and /docs/32-embed-video.

result.answer:
To embed a local or remote MP4 video, use the `snippets/video.html` include with the `fileurl` parameter. When using a local file, provide a root-relative path; the snippet automatically applies `absolute_url`, so do not prepend `baseurl` or use `relative_url`.

```liquid
{% include snippets/video.html fileurl="/assets/mp4/sample.mp4" %}
```

**Next steps:**
1. Upload your video file to the designated directory (e.g., `assets/mp4/`).
2. Ensure the filename and extension match your Liquid code exactly.
3. Commit your changes and check the published result on your live site.

Sources:
[Adding videos](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/32-embed-video)
[Layouts and snippets](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#b-snippets)

question: How do I enable a PhotoSwipe lightbox on a masonry gallery? Is there a page YAML option or Jekyll plugin, and does this work in v2.1.0?
expected: Development after v2.1.0 only. include_cached snippets/masonry.html internal="gallery" photoswipe=true; boolean Liquid include parameter, no page YAML setting or extra plugin. Default disabled, CDN assets load when an image is opened, original image links work without JavaScript. Each gallery isolated; keyboard/Escape/focus restoration and reduced motion. Also works for carousel. Verify opening/closing an image and focus restoration after publishing.

result.answer:
To enable a PhotoSwipe lightbox on a masonry gallery, you must pass the `photoswipe=true` parameter to the `snippets/masonry.html` include.

There is no page-level YAML option or Jekyll plugin for this feature; it is handled via a Liquid parameter within the include. Note that this functionality is part of development after v2.1.0 and is **not available in the released v2.1.0**.

**Example implementation:**
```liquid
{% include_cached snippets/masonry.html internal="gallery" photoswipe=true %}
```

**Next steps:**
1. Ensure you are using a development version (main branch) that supports PhotoSwipe.
2. Verify the lightbox works by opening the live site and clicking an image.

Sources:
* [Masonry and PhotoSwipe documentation](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/31-photoswipe)
* [Layouts and snippets](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#masonry-gallery)

question: Does the HTML theme version marker identify the exact commit and local overrides of my unpinned remote theme? Does v2.2.0 (unreleased) mean I can already install a published 2.2.0 release?
expected: No; inspect remote_theme tag or resolved Gemfile.lock version; marker not exact unpinned commit or local overrides; verify latest publication separately. The unreleased suffix marks a development build: 2.2.0 is an unpublished candidate, v2.1.1-dev labels refer to its planned features, and the latest published release remains v2.1.0. Cite /docs/55-check-theme-version, not /docs/44-custom-head or a relabelled docs index. Gemfile.lock applies to the gem only; remote_theme/build evidence identifies the remote selection.

result.answer:
No, the HTML marker identifies neither the unpinned commit nor any local overrides.

Regarding the version, you cannot install a published 2.2.0 release because it is currently unpublished; v2.1.1-dev labels refer to planned features, not a release. The latest published version is v2.1.0.

To check your current theme version:
*   **Remote theme:** Check the `remote_theme` suffix/build revision.
*   **Gem theme:** Check `chulapa-jekyll` in your `Gemfile.lock`.

Sources:
* [Check theme version](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/55-check-theme-version)

question: I finished the first browser-only Chulapa tutorial. Which guided exercise publishes My photo walk, which file and image does it use, and how do I add its menu link without replacing the existing menu?
expected: Route to https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/59-photo-page-tutorial. Prerequisite: published Chulapa 101 blog and existing assets/img/madrid-at-night.jpg. Create _pages/photo-walk.md with layout default, header_type base, title My photo walk and permalink /photo-walk/; image uses relative_url and meaningful alt text. Add Photo walk with url /photo-walk/ to existing navbar.nav after Categories, retaining other entries and without a repository prefix or second navbar section. Commit to publishing branch, wait for Actions and check the public menu/page/image. Do not claim actual participant success. For insertion code show only the two-line Photo walk item, not a replacement navbar mapping.

result.answer:
The second browser tutorial (the "Photo Walk" tutorial) guides you through publishing a standalone page.

*   **File to create:** `_pages/photo-walk.md`
*   **Image used:** `assets/img/madrid-at-night.jpg`

To add the menu link without replacing your existing configuration, insert only this entry into your `_config.yml` under the `navbar.nav` section, matching the indentation of your other entries:

```yaml
  - title: Photo walk
    url: /photo-walk/
```

**Next steps:**
1. Commit both the new file and the `_config.yml` edits to your publishing branch.
2. Wait for GitHub Actions to succeed.
3. Verify the new link, title, and image by visiting the live site.

Sources:
* [Second browser tutorial](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/59-photo-page-tutorial)
* [Basic editing and publishing](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/00-start)
